question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Near death expereinces are stil near death.
option_2: Near death expriences are still near death.
option_3: Near death experiences are stil near deaath.
option_4: Near death experiences are still near death.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Near death experiences are still near death.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 4 spells every word correctly: experiences (अनुभव), still (अब भी) and death (मृत्यु).

◦ “Experience” = ex + peri + ence; the vowel order is e-r-i-e, so “expereince/exprience” are misspellings.

◦ “Still” always has a double l; “stil” is wrong.

◦ Correct: Near death experiences are still near death.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors — “expereinces” and “stil”.

• Option 2 misspells “experiences” as “expriences” (the letter ‘e’ after ‘p’ is dropped).

• Option 3 has “stil” and “deaath”, both misspelt.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: experience, existence, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, separate.

• Spelling trick: words ending in -ence (existence, occurrence) vs -ance (maintenance, appearance) are a favourite MTS/CHSL trap.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Producing a different component was as simple such launching a new computer program.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as simple such launching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a comparison of equality, and the fixed structure for that is as + adjective + as, never “as … such”. (समान तुलना)

◦ So “as simple such launching” must become “as simple as launching”.

◦ The word after the second “as” is a gerund (“launching”), which correctly parallels the gerund “Producing” at the start.

◦ Correct: Producing a different component was as simple as launching a new computer program.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ‘No error’ is wrong because the sentence clearly contains a comparison error.

• Option 2 “Producing a different component was” is correct — a gerund phrase as subject takes a singular verb.

• Option 4 “a new computer program.” is a correct object phrase.

NOTE

• Comparison patterns: as … as (equality), not so/as … as (negative), -er than / more … than (comparative), the … est / most (superlative).

• “Such as” is used only for examples (fruits such as mango), not for comparison of degree.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The beauty of our landscape is important.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. blemish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Beauty means loveliness, an attractive quality. (सुंदरता)

◦ Blemish means a flaw, spot or defect that spoils appearance. (दाग, दोष) — the exact opposite of beauty.

◦ Correct: The beauty of our landscape is important. — antonym = blemish.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Glamour (आकर्षण) — charm and attractiveness; a synonym, not an antonym.

• Aesthetics (सौंदर्यशास्त्र) — the study or appreciation of beauty; related, not opposite.

• Nobility (कुलीनता) — high moral quality or aristocratic rank; unrelated to beauty.

NOTE

• Synonyms of beauty: elegance, grace, splendour, allure, charm.

• Synonyms of blemish: flaw, stain, defect, taint, imperfection.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

This commodity in clay-coloured material (can’t be used neither as a table mat nor as a table napkin).
option_1: can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin
option_3: can’t be used neither as a table mat but as a table napkin
option_4: can’t be used neither as a table mat or as a table napkin
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• English does not allow a double negative. The sentence already has the negative “can’t”, so “neither … nor” (also negative) cannot follow. (दोहरा नकारात्मक)

◦ With an existing negative verb, the correct correlative pair is either … or.

◦ Correlatives must be parallel: either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

◦ Correct: This commodity in clay-coloured material can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 keeps “can’t … neither … nor”, a double negative, so substitution is required.

• Option 3 wrongly mixes “neither … but”, which is not a correlative pair at all.

• Option 4 wrongly mixes “neither … or”; “neither” must be paired with “nor”.

NOTE

• Correlative pairs: either–or, neither–nor, both–and, not only–but also, whether–or.

• “Neither … nor” is itself negative: “He neither ate nor drank” (never “didn’t neither”).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

People need to made changes in agriculture and land use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. made changes in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Need to” is followed by the to-infinitive, i.e. the bare V1 form of the verb, never the past form V2. (मूल क्रिया रूप)

◦ Hence “to made” is wrong; it must be “to make”.

◦ Correct: People need to make changes in agriculture and land use.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “People need to” is correct — “people” is a plural noun taking the plural verb “need”.

• Option 2 “agriculture and land use.” is a correct object of the preposition “in”.

• Option 3 ‘No error’ is wrong because the verb form after “to” is faulty.

NOTE

• After to (infinitive marker), have to, used to, ought to, able to, going to → always V1.

• Do not confuse with used to / accustomed to / look forward to, where “to” is a preposition and takes V1+ing.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Easiness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gullibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Easiness here carries the sense of being “easy” to fool — a lack of resistance or over-readiness to believe. (सरलता, भोलापन)

◦ Gullibility means the quality of being easily deceived or cheated. (आसानी से बहकावे में आना)

◦ A person of great easiness of mind is an “easy mark”, i.e. gullible.

◦ Correct: His easiness – that is, his gullibility – made him an easy target for con men.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Immunity (प्रतिरक्षा) — resistance to disease or exemption from an obligation.

• Fraternity (भाईचारा) — brotherhood, a group with common interests.

• Indomitability (अजेयता) — the quality of being unconquerable; the opposite in spirit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gullible: credulous, naive, unsuspecting, trusting; antonyms: shrewd, sceptical, astute.

• Related SSC vocabulary: dupe (ठगना), credulity (सहज विश्वास), guile (छल).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Condision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is Condition (स्थिति, दशा), with the ending -tion, not “-sion”.

◦ Nouns formed from verbs ending in -d/-de usually take -sion (decide → decision), but “condition” comes from Latin *conditio* and takes -tion.

◦ Correct: The patient’s condition improved overnight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Busy (व्यस्त) is correctly spelt — note the unusual ‘u’ pronounced /ɪ/.

• Plane (विमान / समतल) is correctly spelt; its homophone is “plain” (सादा).

• Sponge (स्पंज) is correctly spelt — ‘g’ is soft before ‘e’.

NOTE

• ‑tion words: condition, position, addition, ambition, competition.

• ‑sion words: decision, division, occasion, permission, admission.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Government by two rulers or authorities
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Diarchy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diarchy (also spelt dyarchy) = rule by two persons or authorities jointly. (द्वैध शासन)

◦ The prefix di-/dy- means “two” and -archy means “rule”.

◦ In Indian history, the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced diarchy in the provinces.

◦ Correct: Government by two rulers or authorities is called a diarchy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Monarchy (राजतंत्र) — rule by a single king or queen.

• Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही) — government by appointed officials/departments.

• Anarchy (अराजकता) — absence of government; lawlessness.

NOTE

• One-word substitutes for rule: Autocracy (one person, absolute), Oligarchy (a few), Plutocracy (the wealthy), Theocracy (priests/religion), Democracy (the people), Matriarchy/Patriarchy (mother/father-headed).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A case in which the blade of a sword is kept
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sheath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A sheath is the close-fitting cover or case for the blade of a sword, knife or dagger. (म्यान)

◦ Related verb: to unsheathe a sword = to draw it out of its sheath.

◦ Correct: He returned the sword to its sheath.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pantry (भंडार-कक्ष) — a small room where food and crockery are stored.

• Dyke/Dike (बाँध) — an embankment built to hold back water.

• Infirmary (चिकित्सालय) — a place in a school or institution for the sick.

NOTE

• Similar container one-word substitutes: Quiver (case for arrows), Scabbard (sword-case, synonym of sheath), Holster (case for a pistol), Granary (store for grain), Aviary (enclosure for birds), Apiary (place for bees).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.

In another words, most of us / are made by our elders or by our / peers, but leaders are self-directed.
option_2: In another words, most of us
option_3: are made by our elders or by our
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In another words, most of us.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Another” is always followed by a singular countable noun, whereas “words” is plural. (एकवचन के साथ another)

◦ The fixed idiomatic phrase is “in other words” (दूसरे शब्दों में), used to restate something.

◦ Use other before plural nouns: other words, other people, other books.

◦ Correct: In other words, most of us are made by our elders or by our peers, but leaders are self-directed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “peers, but leaders are self-directed.” is grammatically correct.

• Option 3 “are made by our elders or by our” is a correct passive structure.

• Option 4 ‘No error’ is wrong because the phrase “in another words” is faulty.

NOTE

• Another = an + other → singular (another book); Other → plural (other books); The other → the remaining one of two.

• Useful linkers: in other words, that is to say, namely, to put it differently.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

At age 25, she taken her vows and became a nun.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. took her vows.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Taken” is the third form (V3/past participle) and cannot be used alone as the main verb — it needs a helping verb (has/have/had/was).

◦ The sentence has no auxiliary, so the simple past (V2) “took” is required.

◦ Parallelism confirms it: the second verb “became” is simple past, so the first must also be simple past.

◦ Correct: At age 25, she took her vows and became a nun. (व्रत लेना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “take her vows” is present tense and clashes with “became”.

• Option 2 ‘No improvement’ is wrong because “taken” alone is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 “take her vowed” is meaningless — two verbs cannot be joined that way.

NOTE

• Verb forms: take – took – taken; go – went – gone; write – wrote – written.

• V3 is used only with have/has/had (perfect) or be (passive): “She has taken her vows.”

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option ‘no correction required’ if the sentence is correct as given.

They said that they (were understandings) his theory very well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. understood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb “said” is in the past tense, so in indirect speech the reported verb also moves to the past tense. (कालों का अनुक्रम / sequence of tenses)

◦ “Understand” is a stative verb (verb of mental state) and is not normally used in the continuous form.

◦ Hence “were understandings” must become the simple past “understood”.

◦ Correct: They said that they understood his theory very well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “understanding” alone leaves the clause without a finite verb.

• Option 2 ‘No correction required’ is wrong — “were understandings” is doubly faulty (continuous + plural noun form).

• Option 3 “have understand” is wrong; after “have” the V3 “understood” is needed, and the present perfect clashes with “said”.

NOTE

• Stative verbs not used in continuous: know, believe, understand, love, hate, own, seem, want, prefer.

• Reported speech shift: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To sing a different tune
option_1: To change the way one talks about something
option_3: To be able to handle a jolt
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To change the way one talks about something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “to sing a different tune” means to change one’s opinion, attitude or the way one speaks about something, usually reversing an earlier stand. (अपना रुख बदल लेना)

◦ It is often used when circumstances force the change: “He criticised the plan, but once he got the contract he sang a different tune.”

◦ A common variant is “to change one’s tune”.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• “To brag about something” = to blow one’s own trumpet, a different idiom.

• “To be able to handle a jolt” = to take something in one’s stride.

• “To buy or sell something” has no idiomatic link with singing a tune.

NOTE

• Related idioms: to call the tune (to be in control), to face the music (to accept unpleasant consequences), to change horses in midstream (to change plans midway).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

He was ______ in a pool of blood near a neighbour’s house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure “He was ______” needs the present participle (V1+ing) to form the past continuous tense.

◦ The intransitive verb lie (to rest/recline – लेटना) has forms lie – lay – lain – lying; no object follows it.

◦ Since the man is not placing anything, “lay” (to put down – रखना: lay – laid – laid – laying) cannot be used.

◦ Correct: He was lying in a pool of blood near a neighbour’s house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “lain” is the V3 of “lie” and needs “had/has”, not “was”.

• Option 2 “laying” belongs to the transitive verb “lay”, which requires an object.

• Option 4 “lied” is the past of “lie = to tell an untruth” (झूठ बोलना), wrong in meaning here.

NOTE

• Three ‘lie/lay’ verbs: lie–lay–lain–lying (recline), lay–laid–laid–laying (place), lie–lied–lied–lying (tell a lie).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

You have the power ______ the perspective of this nation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to change.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun power is regularly followed by a to-infinitive when it means the ability or authority to do something. (… करने की शक्ति)

◦ The infinitive here works as an adjective phrase qualifying “power”: power to change, power to decide, power to act.

◦ Correct: You have the power to change the perspective of this nation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “changing” would need a preposition (“power of changing”), which is not the natural idiom.

• Option 3 “change” is a bare verb and leaves two finite verbs (“have” and “change”) with no link.

• Option 4 “changed” is the past form and cannot follow the noun “power”.

NOTE

• Nouns commonly followed by to + V1: ability, chance, opportunity, permission, right, decision, wish, attempt, effort.

• Compare: “He has the ability to solve it” but “He is capable of solving it” (preposition + gerund).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Strength training is useful as it avoids large increases in breathing rate and ______ muscle strength.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. improves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes why strength training is useful, so the blank must carry a positive sense.

◦ Improves means makes better or enhances (सुधारता है) — exactly what training does to muscle strength.

◦ Correct: Strength training is useful as it avoids large increases in breathing rate and improves muscle strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Regresses (पीछे लौटना) — returns to a worse or earlier state; contradicts “useful”.

• Distributes (वितरित करना) — to share out; strength is not distributed.

• Degrades (गिराना, घटाना) — lowers quality; the opposite of the required meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of improve: enhance, augment, ameliorate, boost, refine.

• Antonyms: deteriorate, worsen, impair, degrade, diminish.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

A sudden gust of wind hits the window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. blow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A gust is a sudden strong rush of wind. (झोंका)

◦ As a noun, blow likewise means a sudden strong movement of air — “a blow of wind”.

◦ Correct: A sudden gust (= blow) of wind hits the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Cramp (ऐंठन) — a painful involuntary contraction of a muscle.

• Feel (महसूस करना) — to sense by touch or emotion; not a wind word.

• Pump (पंप करना) — a device or the act of forcing liquid/air; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gust: blast, rush, squall, flurry, puff.

• Wind vocabulary for SSC: breeze (light wind), gale (very strong wind), zephyr (a soft gentle breeze), cyclone/typhoon (violent storm).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

With a pinch of salt
option_4: Doubt the truth or value of something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Doubt the truth or value of something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “to take something with a pinch of salt” means to accept a statement with reservation, i.e. not to believe it completely. (पूरी तरह विश्वास न करना)

◦ It suggests scepticism about the truth or importance of what is said.

◦ Example: Take his account of the accident with a pinch of salt — he exaggerates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• “With due respect” is a polite formula used before disagreeing, not this idiom.

• Nefariously (दुष्टतापूर्वक) means wickedly — unrelated.

• “Taken forcefully” is a literal phrase with no idiomatic connection.

NOTE

• The American variant is “with a grain of salt”.

• Related idioms: to take at face value (to believe fully — the opposite), to smell a rat (to suspect something wrong), to cast doubt on (to make people question).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He gave the horse enough room to ______ away from the wagon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. walk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the infinitive marker “to”, so it needs a bare V1 that suits “room … away from the wagon”.

◦ Walk away from is the natural collocation for an animal moving off on foot. (दूर चलकर जाना)

◦ Correct: He gave the horse enough room to walk away from the wagon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “woke” is the past form (V2) of “wake” and cannot follow “to”; it is also illogical here.

• Option 2 “stalk” means to pursue stealthily — a horse given room does not stalk away.

• Option 4 “watch” means to observe and does not fit “away from the wagon”.

NOTE

• Phrasal usage: walk away from (to leave/abandon), walk out on (to desert), walk over (to defeat easily).

• After to as an infinitive marker, always use V1: to go, to walk, to eat.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Lethargy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Attention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lethargy means a lack of energy, sluggishness and drowsy inattentiveness. (सुस्ती, आलस्य)

◦ Attention implies alertness and active mental engagement (ध्यान, सजगता), which is the opposite state of a lethargic mind.

◦ Among the four choices only “attention” denotes alertness, so it is the best available antonym.

◦ Correct: After a cup of coffee his lethargy gave way to keen attention.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Refusal (इनकार) — the act of saying no; the antonym of acceptance.

• Shield (ढाल) — protection or a protective plate; unrelated to energy.

• Existence (अस्तित्व) — the state of being; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lethargy: inertia, torpor, sluggishness, apathy, languor.

• Stronger antonyms often asked: vigour, energy, alertness, vitality, animation.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sustained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is an adjective describing the noun phrase “long-term downturn”, so it must convey continued over time.

◦ Sustained means continuing for an extended period without weakening. (लगातार, निरंतर)

◦ It pairs naturally with “long-term”: a sustained, long-term downturn.

◦ Correct: By contrast, depression is a sustained, long-term downturn in economic activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Curtained — covered with a curtain; makes no sense with a downturn.

• Abstained — refrained from doing something (e.g. voting); it is intransitive and cannot describe a downturn.

• Stained — marked or discoloured; unrelated to economic duration.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sustained: prolonged, continuous, steady, unremitting, persistent.

• Economics vocabulary: recession (a short-term decline), depression (a deep, prolonged recession), stagnation (no growth).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. economies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase is “a downturn in economic activity in one or more ______”, so the blank needs a plural noun meaning national economic systems.

◦ Economies = the wealth and resource systems of countries or regions. (अर्थव्यवस्थाएँ)

◦ A depression is described as spreading across one or more national economies.

◦ Correct: … a sustained, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more economies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Services — one sector of an economy; too narrow, as the downturn covers all activity.

• Autonomies — states of self-government; not units in which economic activity is measured.

• Astronomies — relating to the study of stars; completely irrelevant.

NOTE

• Do not confuse economy (the system / thrift), economic (relating to the economy) and economical (money-saving, cheap).

• Example: an economical car saves fuel; the economic policy shapes the economy.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. severe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure is a comparison: “a more ______ downturn than a recession”, so the blank needs an adjective used with “more … than”.

◦ Severe means intense, harsh or serious. (गंभीर, कठोर)

◦ A depression is by definition deeper and harsher than a recession, so “more severe” is logical.

◦ Correct: A depression is a more severe downturn than a recession.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tamed — domesticated or brought under control; contradicts the idea of a worse downturn.

• Feral — wild, having reverted from domestication; used of animals, not economies.

• Simple — easy or uncomplicated; does not fit a comparison of intensity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of severe: acute, grave, harsh, stringent, intense; antonyms: mild, lenient, gentle.

• Adjectives of two or more syllables take more … than (more severe), not ‘-er’.

Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fluctuations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause says these things “occur around a long-term growth trend” and “involve shifts over time” — so the blank needs a plural noun meaning ups and downs.

◦ Fluctuations are irregular rises and falls in level or amount. (उतार-चढ़ाव)

◦ The business cycle is precisely a series of fluctuations around the trend line.

◦ Correct: The latter refers to fluctuations that occur around a long-term growth trend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Firmness — steadiness or resolve; the opposite of movement around a trend.

• Stability — absence of change; contradicts “shifts over time”.

• Sustainability — the ability to be maintained; also an uncountable idea that does not “occur” around a trend.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fluctuation: variation, oscillation, swing, instability, vacillation.

• Business-cycle phases: expansion (boom) → peak → contraction (recession) → trough → recovery.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. periods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is balanced: “shifts … between ______ of relatively rapid economic growth … and periods of relative stagnation or decline”.

◦ Parallel structure demands the same noun in both halves, so the blank must be periods (अवधि, कालखंड).

◦ The preposition “between” also requires a plural noun, which “periods” supplies.

◦ Correct: … shifts over time between periods of relatively rapid economic growth … and periods of relative stagnation or decline.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Perpetually is an adverb (“constantly”) and cannot follow the preposition “between”.

• Perpetuity means an endless duration; it is singular and does not fit “between … and periods”.

• Prods means pokes or urges; meaningless in an economic time context.

NOTE

• Between is used for two items/groups; among for more than two.

• Parallelism rule: items joined by and/or/but must be of the same grammatical form (noun–noun, verb–verb, phrase–phrase).
